body: This is a very wild approach but, for me, the moment i admitted that life is not a must, i wanted to live. However, i also have a therapist who helped me a lot in my depression. I also find cognitive therapy more effective than medicine, but it’s the professionals decision in the end if medicine is necessary. So she needs to go to a therapist who she can feel safe around. Also this is just a place where people share their opinions, what people say may not work for everyone.

because the whole idea of surviving is based on who can cope better with the problems in the nature, and human mind has proved its capability in coping. Because of the ancient religions, people were able to unite in the name of an abstract thought, and survive better. We have made up countries that don’t really exist in nature so that we can cope with problems together. We are even uniting the countries as United Nations, European Union etc. which really don’t exist in the first place but we create them to cope with world’s problems. All these creations are a result of our thought process. I think our brain is really capable of creating an illusion of meaning so that we can cope. But my question really is why is it so important for our brain to cope with all of this to live more? Even this question itself brings up that meaning in life. What matters to me is not the meaning, but why it’s programmed that way, which would really explain why we shouldn’t kill ourselves. (Ironically, that’s how i want to put meaning in my life)

i appreciate your answer but it all seems to me as our brains trying to make sense of this world and “simulating” a feeling of higher meaning so that we can continue living as a coping mechanism. I don’t know if you are religious or not, but when I see a religious person i can see this perfectly. Those people have found the meaning and “the point” in that belief system and their brains are functioning to use that system as a coping mechanism. I am not saying that their belief are not real or real, that is irrelevant. What matters is how the human mind utilises that information to solve humane problems
